messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Bug uncovered by histogram
parts:
Hi,

it seems binning is problematic when only negative values are present:
> x = c(-4.638178, -4.941915, -4.440807, -3.722744, -4.038494,
> -4.235646, -3.328221, -3.967511, -4.764347, -3.497780, -3.904317)
> qplot(x, geom="histogram")
stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust
this.
Error: position_stack requires non-overlapping x intervals
> x=-x
> qplot(x, geom="histogram")
stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust
this.

Other symptom:
> x=-100:-1
> qplot(x, geom="histogram")
stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust
this.
Error in if (any(diff(intervals) < -1e-06)) { :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
> x=-x
> qplot(x, geom="histogram")
stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust
this.

This is with the latest and hotest ggplot from git. A change to what
seemed a syntax error in position_collide solves it:

diff --git a/R/position-collide.r b/R/position-collide.r
index e64717e..8191c76 100644
--- a/R/position-collide.r
+++ b/R/position-collide.r
@@ -29,7 +29,7 @@ collide <- function(data, width = NULL, name,
strategy, check.width = TRUE) {

# Check for overlap
data <- data[order(data$xmin), ]
- intervals <- as.numeric(t(unique(data[c("xmin", "xmax")])))
+ intervals <- as.numeric(t(unique(data[c("xmin", "xmax"),])))
intervals <- intervals[!is.na(intervals)] / max(intervals)
if (any(diff(intervals) < -1e-6)) {
stop(name, " requires non-overlapping x intervals", call. = FALSE)

JiHO

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Bug uncovered by histogram
parts:
Hi Jiho,

Thanks for the bug report, it's now fixed in the development version.

This should have made any difference - they're both equivalent ways of
indexing a data frame.
>   intervals <- intervals[!is.na(intervals)] / max(intervals)

What you really need is this (or something similar)

intervals <- scale(intervals[!is.na(intervals)])

Detecting overlaps with floating point numbers really is a nightmare :(

Hadley
